chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hajjaj, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:
I saw Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them) when they raised their heads from the second prostration, they rose (to stand) and did not sit.
ai.seo_question: What did the Imams do after the second prostration in prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the distinct prayer practice of the Imams, specifically their omission of the sitting position (qa'dah) after the second prostration. This detail is central to the Shia jurisprudential debate regarding the number of sitting positions in the four-rak'ah prayer, distinguishing the Shia view from the Sunni practice of two qa'dahs. It underscores the emphasis on following the Prophetic tradition as interpreted and practiced by the Ahl al-Bayt.
